summary: Test verified the live BiliDili RF-3 schema/migration path after accepted Core+Plugin repairs, but could not prove same-rescanId live idempotency because the public MCP rescan route never opened a new deep_mining_round for any explicit RF-3 rescanId. Live DB backup was captured before probing. After alembic_status, deep_mining_rounds gained nullable rescan_id and the partial unique index deep_mining_rounds_rescan_unique; DB stayed knowledge_entries=42 and coverage_ledger=30. Three real MCP rescan probes completed without stale empty-session BOOTSTRAP regression: an initial same-rescanId converged probe, a minimal-gap probe with architecture target 35/networking-api target 30, and a controllerAuthorized produceSession probe. The latter two returned executionDimensions=2 and produceDimensions=2, but response/logs still reported coverageAdvisory=converged and released the empty session; SQL showed count(*)=0 for every explicit RF-3 rescanId and all existing rounds retained rescan_id NULL. Source attribution points to AlembicPlugin knowledge-rescan.ts:593-604, where coverageAdvisory.shouldStop=true sets noActionableRescanWork and skips openDeepMiningRound; therefore the live ledger write/reflow path with rescanId remains unproven and needs Plugin/Core review.

risks: RF-3 live idempotency is not accepted: same-rescanId duplicate prevention could not be observed because the live public MCP route never wrote a non-null rescan_id row.
Completion/reflow preserving rescan_id is not accepted: reflow cannot be proven without an opened RF-3 round carrying rescan_id.

Likely owner is AlembicPlugin public alembic_rescan workflow/advisory ordering or AlembicCore advisor verdict behavior: route can return produceDimensions=2 while coverageAdvisory.shouldStop=true, causing openDeepMiningRound to be skipped.

Recommended next repair: make openDeepMiningRound run when deepMining has execution/produce dimensions, or adjust coverageAdvisory so shouldStop is not true for produceDimensions>0; then redispatch Test for two live MCP rescan calls with the same explicit rescanId and SQL count exactly 1.
